name: Carter G. Woodson Home National Historic Site
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: The Carter G. Woodson Home National Historic Site in Washington, D.C., preserves the residence and workplace of Dr. Carter G. Woodson (1875–1950), the scholar known as the "Father of Black History." Woodson, the second African American to earn a Ph.D. from Harvard University (after W.E.B. Du Bois), founded the Association for the Study of Negro Life and History in 1915, established the Journal of Negro History in 1916, and created Negro History Week in 1926 — which later became Black History Month. He lived and worked in the Shaw neighborhood rowhouse from 1922 until his death in 1950. The site was designated a national historic site in 2006.
